question: Can a frozen pretrained text-to-image diffusion model be given new grounding inputs (boxes, keypoints, reference images, spatial maps) without forgetting its concept knowledge, and generalise to unseen concepts?
hypothesis: Freezing the pretrained weights and injecting grounding through new gated self-attention layers preserves concept knowledge and lets box grounding generalise to open-world concepts even when trained on COCO only.
contributions: A new text2img method that endows grounding controllability over existing text2img diffusion models.
By preserving pretrained weights and gradually integrating new localization layers, achieves open-world grounded text2img with bounding box inputs.
Zero-shot layout2img performance significantly outperforms prior state of the art.

method.summary: Freeze all weights of a pretrained latent diffusion model (LDM trained on LAION, or Stable Diffusion) and insert new trainable gated self-attention layers into each Transformer block that attend over visual tokens concatenated with grounding tokens. A grounding token is an MLP over the text (or image) embedding of an entity and the Fourier embedding of its box. A scheduled sampling scheme turns the gate off after a fraction tau of steps.
method.task: grounded text-to-image generation (layout2img, open-set box grounding, keypoints, spatial maps, inpainting)

training.objective: original denoising objective ||eps - f(z_t, t, y)||^2 over new parameters only; gated self-attention v = v + beta*tanh(gamma)*TS(SelfAttn([v, h^e])), gamma initialised 0, beta = 1 in training
training.steps: 100k iterations (COCO experiments, LDM); 400k iterations (scaled data, LDM); 500K iterations (Stable Diffusion)
training.regularisation: caption and grounding tokens randomly dropped with 10% probability for classifier-free guidance

other.spatial_condition_encoder: convnext-tiny on 256x256 input, 8x8 features flattened to 64 tokens; extra input to UNet first conv, which is trainable
other.image_embedding_norm: CLIP image features projected into text space and normalised to 28.7

inference.decoding: diffusion sampling; scheduled sampling with beta = 1 for first tau*T steps and 0 afterwards
inference.samples: 30K images generated for COCO evaluation; 5000 images per object size for inpainting
inference.prompting: caption plus grounded entities; null caption for detection-only data

parameters.tau: 0.2 in Fig 7 examples; default beta = 1 throughout

limits: Keypoint grounding learned on humans does not transfer to non-humanoid categories such as cat or lamp even with scheduled sampling (Appendix G).
Constant beta=1 sampling sometimes gives lower image quality than the original text2img model; scheduled sampling is a trade-off.
Baseline text2img models cannot take boxes, so YOLO score is reported only for fine-tuned LDM as reference.
No seeds, repeat runs or significance tests; compute for scaled runs and several dataset sizes not stated.
Pseudo-caption ablation: authors leave text-encoder fine-tuning or better prompts for future work.
Attention maps in early UNet layers are uninterpretable, attributed to lack of positional embeddings in visual tokens.
